hindi: अपने पक्ष में शत्रु द्वारा प्रयुक्त दूषी-विष और गर का प्रतिकार।
english: Remedy, in one's own party, against the tainting poisons and garas employed by the enemy.
notes: dūṣī-viṣa is taken as 'tainting poison' (a class of poison); gara is kept as gara (a compounded poison). Division read here: dūṣī-viṣa + gara (two members, as in the gloss); alternative: three members dūṣī, viṣa, gara.

words.gram: compound members (continued in the next token); dvandva list

words.gloss: mixed with a decoction of the herbs in the previous token and of punarnavā, śveta and vāraṇa
mixed with candana, sālā, vṛkī and lohita
of those to be used by the king

hindi: श्लेष्मातक, कपित्थ, दन्ती, दन्त, शठ, गोजी, शिरीष, पाटली, बला, स्योनाग, पुनर्नवा, श्वेत और वारण के काढ़े से युक्त तथा चन्दन, साला, वृकी और लोहित से युक्त धोने का जल राजा के उपभोग्य के लिए, स्त्रियों के लिए गुह्य का प्रक्षालन, और सेना के लिए विष का प्रतिकार है।
english: Washing water mixed with a decoction of śleṣmātaka, kapittha, danti, danta, śaṭha, goji, śirīṣa, pāṭalī, balā, syonāga, punarnavā, śveta and vāraṇa, and mixed with candana, sālā, vṛkī and lohita: [it is] for those to be used by the king, a washing of the private parts for women, and a remedy against poison for the army.
notes: All the names are drug names, kept as printed; no identification given. The word-by-word listing of the first token is only the order of the printed members; 'danti' and 'danta' may be one name 'dantī-danta' and 'śveta' may be 'śvetā' or an adjective 'white'. 'sālā' and 'lohita' (red?) are uncertain. 'balā-syonāga' split as two members. 'rāja-upabhogyānām' has no noun: those things (or persons) to be used by the king. The three datives/genitives (king's articles, women, army) are read as three uses; the closing 'viṣa-pratīkāraḥ' may govern all three. The editors' doubt mark '(?)' on 'yuktaṃ' is kept in src; 'yuktam' is read plainly. 'danta-śaṭha' may be a single plant name (so 'danta' and 'śaṭha' would not be separate members); 'syonāga' may be a variant of 'syonāka'. Both are only possible; the split follows the edition's dots. The genitives 'rāja-upabhogyānām', 'strīṇām', 'senāyāḥ' are read as objective genitives of nejana / prakṣālana / pratīkāra respectively; the scope of 'viṣa-pratīkāraḥ' (army only, or all three) is not settled, so confidence stays low.
lines_deva: श्लेष्मातक.कपित्थ.दन्ति.दन्त.शठ.गोजि.शिरीष.पाटली.बलास्योनाग.- पुनर्.नवा.श्वेत.वारण.क्वाथ.युक्तं(?) चन्दन.साला.वृकी.लोहित.युक्तं नेजन.उदकं राज.उपभोग्यानां गुह्य.प्रक्षालनं स्त्रीणाम्, सेनायाश् च विष.प्रतीकारः
lines_iast: śleṣmātaka.kapittha.danti.danta.śaṭha.goji.śirīṣa.pāṭalī.balāsyonāga.- punar.navā.śveta.vāraṇa.kvātha.yuktaṃ(?) candana.sālā.vṛkī.lohita.yuktaṃ nejana.udakaṃ rāja.upabhogyānāṃ guhya.prakṣālanaṃ strīṇām, senāyāś ca viṣa.pratīkāraḥ

words.gloss: mixed with the bile of the spotted deer, mongoose, peacock and godhā
sindu, vārita, varaṇa, vāruṇī, taṇḍulīyaka, tip of śataparva, piṇḍītaka
remover of the ill effect of madana

hindi: चित्तीदार मृग, नेवला, मोर और गोधा के पित्त से युक्त महीराजी का चूर्ण तथा सिन्दु, वारित, वरण, वारुणी, तण्डुलीयक, शतपर्व के अग्र और पिण्डीतक का योग मदन के दोष को हरने वाला है।
english: Powder of mahīrājī mixed with the bile of the spotted deer, mongoose, peacock and godhā, [and] the compound of sindu, vārita, varaṇa, vāruṇī, taṇḍulīyaka, the tip of śataparva and piṇḍītaka, [is] the remover of the ill effect of madana.
notes: The predicate 'haraḥ' is masculine and agrees only with 'yogaḥ'; the neuter 'cūrṇam' does not agree with it, so its relation is uncertain; it is read here as a second subject, and both are taken as removers of madana's ill effect. 'sindu-vārita' could be the single name 'sinduvāra' plus 'vārita'; kept as printed. 'nīla-kaṇṭha' literally 'blue-necked', rendered peacock; 'godhā' is a lizard name, kept. 'śata-parva-agra' = tip of the hundred-jointed (plant). Drug names kept without identification. 'nīla-kaṇṭha' is also a name of other blue-necked birds (e.g. the blue jay); 'peacock' is the common lexical sense, kept with that reservation.

words.gloss: of the decoctions of the roots of sṛgālavinnā, madana, sindu, vārita, varaṇa and vāraṇavallī
removing the ill effect of madana

hindi: सृगालविन्ना, मदन, सिन्दु, वारित, वरण और वारणवल्ली की जड़ों के काढ़ों में से किसी एक का अथवा सबका दूध मिलाया हुआ पेय मदन के दोष को हरने वाला है।
english: A drink, mixed with milk, of any one or of all together of the decoctions of the roots of sṛgālavinnā, madana, sindu, vārita, varaṇa and vāraṇavallī removes the ill effect of madana.

text_flags.why: possible: 'valī' for 'vallī' (creeper); a drug name, so only suspected

notes: Drug names kept without identification. 'madana' is both a drug in the list and the thing whose ill effect is removed. The word list, English and Hindi follow the suggested spelling 'vallī' (vāraṇa-vallī); the printed 'valī' is kept in src. The flag is only possible.
lines_deva: सृगाल.विन्ना.मदन.सिन्दु.वारित.वरण.वारण.वली.मूल.कषायाणाम् अन्यतमस्य समस्तानां वा क्षीर.युक्तं पानं मदन.दोष.हरम्
lines_iast: sṛgāla.vinnā.madana.sindu.vārita.varaṇa.vāraṇa.valī.mūla.kaṣāyāṇām anyatamasya samastānāṃ vā kṣīra.yuktaṃ pānaṃ madana.doṣa.haram

words.gloss: sesame oil [prepared with] kaiḍarya and pūti

hindi: कैडर्य और पूति वाला तिल का तेल उन्माद को हरने वाला है; नाक के द्वारा किया जाने वाला कर्म।
english: Sesame oil [prepared with] kaiḍarya and pūti removes madness; [it is] an action through the nose.
notes: 'kaiḍarya-pūti' may be one name or two (pūti literally 'foul-smelling'); kept as two members. 'nastaḥ' = 'through the nose' (ind.); 'nastaḥ-karma' is the nasal application. 'sesame oil [prepared with]' is the relation of a compound, bracketed because no verb or word states it.

hindi: प्रियङ्गु और नक्तमाल का योग कुष्ठ को हरने वाला है।
english: A compound of priyaṅgu and naktamāla removes kuṣṭha.
notes: kuṣṭha here is the affliction (a skin disease); the same word in the next unit is a drug name. Drug names kept.

hindi: कुष्ठ और लोध्र का योग पाक और शोष को नष्ट करने वाला है।
english: A compound of kuṣṭha and lodhra destroys pāka and śoṣa.
notes: Here kuṣṭha is read as a drug name. pāka (ripening) and śoṣa (drying up) are kept as the Sanskrit terms; they may be read as a single compound 'drying up after ripening'. Sense not fixed.

words.gloss: powder of kaṭaphala, dravantī and vilaṅga

hindi: कटफल, द्रवन्ती और विलङ्ग का चूर्ण, नाक के द्वारा किया जाने वाला कर्म, सिर के रोग को हरने वाला है।
english: Powder of kaṭaphala, dravantī and vilaṅga, an action through the nose, removes head-disease.
notes: 'kaṭa-phala' kept as one drug name though it might be 'kaṭu-phala'; not flagged as it is a name. Drug names kept.

words.gloss: priyaṅgu, mañjiṣṭhāta, garalā, kṣāra, samadhuka, haridrā and kṣaudra
of those made unconscious by rope, water, poison, blow or fall

hindi: प्रियङ्गु, मञ्जिष्ठात, गरला, क्षार, समधुक, हरिद्रा और क्षौद्र का योग रस्सी, जल, विष, प्रहार और पतन से संज्ञाहीन हुए लोगों को फिर से वापस लाने के लिए है।
english: A compound of priyaṅgu, mañjiṣṭhāta, garalā, kṣāra, samadhuka, haridrā and kṣaudra [is] for bringing back again those made unconscious by rope, water, poison, blow or fall.

text_flags.why: possible: the same letters can be re-divided into known drug names (mañjiṣṭhā, tagara, lākṣā, rasa, madhuka); the printed division gives the unusual 'mañjiṣṭhāta' and 'garalā' (garala = poison)
orthography: h written for visarga; not a real error

notes: The printed members are followed literally in words; the re-division in text_flags is only possible. 'kṣāra' = alkali, 'kṣaudra' = honey are not translated in the list because they may be drug names. 'sa-madhuka' may mean 'with madhuka'. The relation 'made unconscious by' is the compound's sense (rope = hanging, etc., not stated). The dative states purpose only; 'punaḥ-pratyānayana' literally 'bringing back again'. Checked letter for letter: 'mañjiṣṭhā-tagara-lākṣā-rasa-madhuka' gives the same string as the printed 'mañjiṣṭhāta.garalā.kṣāra.samadhuka'; the translation keeps the printed division, so 'mañjiṣṭhāta' and 'garalā' are unattested names kept as printed, not identified.

hindi: मनुष्यों के लिए अक्ष की मात्रा, गौओं और घोड़ों के लिए दुगुनी, हाथियों और ऊँटों के लिए चौगुनी।
english: For men, the measure of an akṣa; for cattle and horses, twofold; fourfold for elephants and camels.
notes: The thing measured (the compound of the previous unit) is not stated; 'akṣa' is a unit of weight, kept. 'gava' is the compound form of 'go' (cattle); 'hasty.uṣṭrāṇām' is hasti + uṣṭrāṇām.
lines_deva: मनुष्याणाम् अक्ष.मात्रम्, गव.अश्वानां द्वि.गुणम्, चतुर्.गुणं हस्त्य्.उष्ट्राणाम्
lines_iast: manuṣyāṇām akṣa.mātram, gava.aśvānāṃ dvi.guṇam, catur.guṇaṃ hasty.uṣṭrāṇām

hindi: और इनका सुवर्ण-गर्भ मणि सब विषों को हरने वाला है।
english: And a jewel of these, having gold within, removes all poison.
notes: The referent of 'eṣām' is not fixed by the line: it may point to the men and animals of the previous unit or to the ingredients named earlier; 'jewel of these' is kept literal.

words.gloss: of jīvantī, śvetā, muṣkaka, puṣpa and vandāka

hindi: जीवन्ती, श्वेता, मुष्कक, पुष्प और वन्दाक की तथा अक्षीव पर उत्पन्न अश्वत्थ की मणि सब विषों को हरने वाली है।
english: The jewel of jīvantī, śvetā, muṣkaka, puṣpa and vandāka, [and] of the aśvattha born on an akṣīva, removes all poison.
notes: Two genitive phrases stand side by side without 'ca'; read as two sources of the jewel. Alternative: 'vandāka' (parasite) of each of the four preceding plants, and 'puṣpa' may be 'flower'. 'akṣīva' kept as a tree name; 'aśvattha' as the tree name. No identification.

hindi: उनसे लेपे हुए वाद्यों का शब्द विष का नाश करने वाला है; लेपे हुए ध्वज या पताका को देखकर विषमुक्त हो जाता है।
english: The sound of musical instruments anointed with them destroys poison; having seen an anointed banner or flag, [one] becomes free of poison.
notes: 'taiḥ' refers back to the earlier preparations; 'lipta' is anointed with those, as the line implies. The subject of 'bhavati' is not stated ('one', here the poisoned person). 'tūrya' = musical instrument (drum etc.).
lines_deva: लिप्त.ध्वजं पताकां वा दृष्ट्वा भवति निर्विषः
lines_iast: lipta.dhvajaṃ patākāṃ vā dṛṣṭvā bhavati nirviṣaḥ

words.gloss: tainters by poison, smoke and water

hindi: इनसे अपनी सेनाओं का और फिर अपना प्रतिकार करके शत्रुओं पर विष, धूम और जल के दूषकों का प्रयोग करे।
english: Having made a remedy with these for his own troops and then for himself, he should employ against enemies the tainters of poison, smoke and water.
notes: 'viṣa-dhūma-ambu-dūṣaṇān' may also be read as 'poison, smoke and water-pollutions' (things that taint) or 'taintings'; kept as agents that taint. The subject is the king (not stated). 'dūṣaṇān' is masculine accusative plural, whereas 'dūṣaṇa' is normally neuter (one would expect 'dūṣaṇāni'); the relation of poison, smoke and water to 'dūṣaṇa' (tainting by them, or tainting of them) is not settled.
